questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Does not matter much for whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because other drivers may not see you if you are in the wrong position.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because other drivers may not see you if you are in the wrong position.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better and be seen by others. Proper positioning also protects you from wind blasts created by other vehicles.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire controls your steering, which affects your balance.
A flat front tire will stop your front brake from working.
A flat front tire will stop you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire controls your steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering harder. This affects your ability to balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes when you need to stop.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off of other vehicles better.
You will be able to stop quickly.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If a problem appears, you will have more time to react and more room to move safely.

questions.question: When being followed closely by another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that encourages the other vehicle to pass you. Going faster will only make them follow you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Make sure the transmission is in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: Reflective clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn at night.
Should only be worn during the day.
Should be worn at all times, day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be worn at all times, day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, no matter what time it is.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagon signs are always stop signs. When you see one, come to a complete stop. Look for other traffic and pedestrians. Only go when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see and be seen by others.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Wearing gloves while riding gives you a better grip and protects your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong, durable material.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. A smart rider changes position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center lane position is usually the safest.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked often by all riders.
Be used only by the lead rider.
Not be checked often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked often by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and makes sure the group stays together.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: For riding, wear sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: It is hard to ride right after rain starts because:

options.text: Some drivers may not react quickly to the rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement is especially slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away from the road, and it mixes with the water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: Wind noise:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Exposure to wind noise over time can cause permanent hearing damage. It is recommended to wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle for safety:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always do a thorough safety check of your motorcycle before you ride. A small problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than a small problem on a car.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road edge shows:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the road edge marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the rear and front brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: When riding a motorcycle, wear protective clothing. Good protection includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and leather gloves with all fingers covered. Cover as much skin as possible when riding.

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. What do they indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle sways from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When should you NOT flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are slowing down faster than others expect
When you are slowing down where others won't expect it
When people are walking on a nearby sidewalk

questions.correctAnswerText: When people are walking on a nearby sidewalk
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is smaller than a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down where drivers may not expect it. Also flash your brake light when slowing faster than other drivers expect. Do not flash it at pedestrians on sidewalks.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people think helmets limit vision, but this is not true. A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Which material provides the best crash protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Sturdy leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in a crash. Wear long pants and jackets made of these materials when riding.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph. These include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using the correct braking technique is important for safe riding.
